guiding_question: Can federated learning preserve predictive performance relative to centralized training?
supported_conclusion: The three conditions achieved closely grouped predictive performance across three seeds.
interpretation_boundary: Use comparability rather than superiority language; n=3 seeds.

guiding_question: Does label-skew non-IID training cause persistent predictive failure?
supported_conclusion: The tested non-IID condition converged to strong performance without persistent late collapse.
interpretation_boundary: Applies to the tested five-client label-skew configuration.

guiding_question: How do Grad-CAM explanations change across communication rounds?
supported_conclusion: Explanations changed strongly early and became increasingly stable relative to Round 50.
interpretation_boundary: Later adjacent intervals are not pooled when checkpoint spacing differs.

guiding_question: Do models with similar predictions produce similar spatial explanations?
supported_conclusion: Prediction agreement was high while centralized-versus-federated Grad-CAM similarity remained moderate.
interpretation_boundary: Similar predictions do not imply equivalent spatial reasoning.

guiding_question: How similar are IID and non-IID federated explanations?
supported_conclusion: IID and non-IID explanations were consistently more similar to each other than either was to centralized training.
interpretation_boundary: Do not claim centralized is systematically closer to IID or non-IID.
